patch.roundTrip: Forward and inverse patches exactly reproduce current/frozen mixed-collector bytes.

scope: One optional first-failing known-feature mesh probe inside each original-public fixture inventory; no additional attachment, raw mesh export, geometry repair or tolerance change.
sourceBinding: Original fixture SHA256 and original feature UUID must match; probe node must be a known sampled mesh with matching vertexCount.
Source dimensions/transform/local bounds equal exact Float32 conversion of pinned original public feature; no numeric tolerance.
Original world bbox is recomputed from source polygon corners or eight original local bbox corners in the identical Double operation order.
worldPoint to sourceLocalPoint follows exact NativeCameraTransform inverse/apply Double arithmetic; arbitrary independently fabricated residual is rejected.
Lower/upper, epsilon64*2^-23*scale, positive residual and first violated axis obey the unchanged production inequality.
Exported bbox contains recorded point; all numeric fields finite and bounded; optional probeFailure is fixed enum and mutually exclusive with probe.
Probe/probeFailure requires existing adapterFailure sourceGeometryMismatch; unknown fields, raw vertex/triangle arrays and private text remain rejected.

inverseSourceEvidence.verification: Independently fetched and inspected exact inverse/apply left-associative Double expressions.

limitations: Synthetic Python schema/predicate tests are not native ModelIO/RoomPlan execution.
Native SIMD Float mesh-to-world multiplication is retained as observed data; collector does not impose a guessed Double equivalent.
No all-vertex or triangle buffer is exported, so collector does not independently prove first vertex or whole-mesh bounds; bounded test producer owns that observation.
A geometry diagnostic cannot authorize physical guidance or convert a failed test into a pass.
The inventory/probe is a second export of the same admitted public input; it does not prove byte-identical geometry to the separate adapter export whose failure is recorded.
